title: wordchain
description: Everything wordchain.toml may say about the disc: the ground it draws on, the eight distances that place things, and the wheel that maps 26 letters to 26 hues. Every key is optional and anything left out keeps its default. Kept in step with src/wordchain/config.py by tools/check_schema.py.

theme.description: The ground the figure draws on. The two are complete palettes rather than one inverted, and `build --theme` overrides this.

enumValues: 4856 faint curves read as light against a dark ground, which is why it is the default.
The same figure on a pale ground, with the letter wheel's saturation up 0.07 and its value down 0.28.

geometry.description: Where the disc puts things. The good value for each depends on the category: 895 animals and 60 flowers do not want the same label size or the same curve pull.

pull.description: How far a chord's control points sit toward the centre, as a fraction of the radius. Curves leave each node heading inwards, so a chord reads as the pair of letters it joins rather than as a line across the disc. Lower bows harder.

pull_dense.description: The same for the word disc once it passes 150 words, where the wider middle of `pull` would read as fog.

label_radius.description: Where the word labels start, as a fraction of the dot ring.

label_pt.description: Label size in points. It also sets the canvas, because a label's length is fixed in inches by the font and only a wider figure buys it room along the ring, so raising this grows the figure rather than crowding it.

leading.description: Clear space each label demands along the ring, in multiples of its own size. It decides when two neighbours count as touching, to the same effect.

wedge_band.description: Room kept outside the labels for the wedge letter, in data units.

glyph_width.description: Mean glyph width as a fraction of the font size. It only reserves space, so erring high costs a little margin and nothing else.

disc_limit.description: Half the width of the chord diagram's axes, in data units, and the conversion the word disc's canvas is solved in. The word disc works out its own limit.

palette.description: The wheel that maps 26 letters to 26 hues. Leave the whole table out and the theme keeps its own. Name a preset, or give the numbers for a single arc, and never both: a preset can hold two arcs, as duotone does, so there is no honest way to layer one arc's worth of keys over it.

preset.description: A named wheel, and the shorter of the two ways to set one: naming a preset is one string edit where the arc below is five. spectrum is what the theme brings on its own, so naming it changes nothing. Every preset is tuned against the dark ground; on the light one the same wheel is drawn with saturation up 0.07 and value down 0.28.

enumValues: Two short arcs, warm for A-M and cool for N-Z, so every curve crossing between the halves of the alphabet reads as a crossing.
A quarter turn through the reds and oranges.
The full turn with A and Z separated, and the luma spread cut from 1.86x to 1.38x.
The full turn the tool has always drawn.
A quarter turn through the greens and blues.

hue_start.description: Where the letters start on the colour circle. Zero is meaningful here: it is the top of the circle, which is where the wheel has always started.

hue_span.description: How much of the circle the letters cover. A span of exactly 1 closes it, which puts A and Z one step apart and makes them read as the same hue; a little under 1 separates them. A quarter turn gives up telling adjacent letters apart and buys a disc that reads as one object.

saturation.description: Fixed across the wheel, so all 26 letters stay equally visible against the ground.

value.description: Fixed across the wheel, for the same reason as the saturation.

equalise.description: How far each letter's value is pulled towards a common brightness, from 0 for none to 1 for equal. Zero is meaningful here, and means no correction. A fixed-saturation wheel spans about 1.9x in luma, and every bundle is drawn at one alpha, so a yellow overwhelms a blue at equal weight. Correction can only take brightness away, so 1 sends the greens olive and 0.65 is about as far as they stay green.

allOf.$comment: A preset and the arc's own numbers are mutually exclusive. Forbidding each key in turn, rather than negating the whole table, is what makes an editor underline the offending line instead of printing the clause back at you.
